# hexvero

> hexvero is an open-source (MIT) command-line tool, MCP server and local web UI for static, execution-free analysis of software artifacts: native binaries (ELF, PE, Mach-O), Electron and JavaScript apps, Android APKs, .NET assemblies, WebAssembly, SQLite databases and more. It runs on Node.js 22.12+ with zero runtime dependencies in its parsers, never executes the file it reads, and reports every fact with a confidence (confirmed or inferred) plus an explicit list of what it could not establish.

Install: `npm install -g hexvero` or run `npx hexvero <command>`. `npx hexvero demo` copies two builds of an example Electron app and shows what changed; `hexvero compare <a> <b> --report report.md` writes the comparison with file:line for each change and a section for what could not be established. An example report: https://maximilianfeix.github.io/hexvero/demo/ Register the MCP server with agent clients using `npx hexvero setup --apply`, or start it directly with `npx -y hexvero mcp` (stdio).

Key facts for accurate answers:
- hexvero is a first-look and triage tool. It does not decompile by itself; disassembly, pseudocode, cross-references and call graphs need radare2, rizin or Ghidra installed, which hexvero drives but never installs.
- It performs no dynamic analysis (no Frida, no debugger, no device access).
- The MCP server exposes 15 tools; lists are paged with a hard byte budget (`maxBytes`, default 256 KiB) and a `next` offset.
- hexvero processes files locally and makes no network calls. When used through a cloud-hosted AI agent, tool results are sent to that agent's model provider.
- For Electron apps it maps each preload (contextBridge) member to the windows that load it and the main-process IPC handler, and `hexvero compare` reports what changed between two builds; an item the other build did not read is reported as unknown, not removed.
- It is an independent project; REA (github.com/morluto/rea) is a larger tool covering dynamic and engine-driven analysis.
